title: High Intensity Exercise Therapy for Bone Density in Postmenopausal Women
author: Takashi Kitagawa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bucinsue

steps.title: Search for Relevant Literature
steps.instruction: Conduct a comprehensive search for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing high intensity exercise therapy for bone density in postmenopausal women across multiple databases and registries.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog, and MEDLINE via ProQuest Dialog using the specific search strategies detailed in Appendixes 1-6.
Search for unpublished or ongoing trials via the WHO International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov.
Request unpublished or additional data directly from original study authors.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Identify eligible studies based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria through a multi-stage review process.

substeps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts independently (Reviewers K.H. and T.D.).
Assess full texts for eligibility. Resolve divergences between reviewers through discussion or arbitration by a third reviewer (T.K.).

Apply inclusion criteria: RCTs of postmenopausal women with osteoporotic conditions (T-score < 1 SD or < 80% of young adult mean), including those treated with or without drug therapy, where outcomes include BMD of lumbar spine and femoral neck.
Apply exclusion criteria: Diseases affecting bone metabolism, uncontrolled cardiovascular disease, cognitive disorder (MMSE < 24), or recent surgery/injury to lower extremity or lower back.

Categorize interventions: 'High intensity' (1RM ≥ 80% for ≤ 6 reps; GRF ≥ 4x body weight; stiff-legged landing jumps; or aerobics load > 4x body weight) vs 'Moderate intensity' (1RM 65-80% for 8-15 reps; GRF 2-4x body weight; heel drop exercise; or aerobics load < 4x body weight). If multiple exercises are used, allocate based on the highest intensity.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Independently extract data from eligible studies using a standardized collection form.

substeps.instruction: Use a pre-checked form validated with 10 randomly selected studies.

Extract general characteristics (ID, date, title, authors, source), study design (RCT type, participants, exclusion criteria), population, interventions (frequency, intensity, type, time, control group details, follow-up period), and outcomes (BMD changes of lumbar spine/femoral neck, adverse events).
Extract details required for risk of bias assessment.
Resolve extraction discrepancies via discussion or arbitration by T.K.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the risk of bias for each included study using the Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool.

substeps.instruction: Review each study against five criteria independently (K.H. and T.D.).
Record results as 'low risk of bias', 'unclear risk of bias', or 'high risk of bias'.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or arbitration by S.Y.

steps.title: Analyze Data and Treatment Effects
steps.instruction: Pool data and calculate treatment effects for primary and secondary outcomes.

substeps.instruction: Pool mean differences and 95% CIs for continuous variables: BMD of lumbar spine (DEXA), BMD of femoral neck (DEXA), quality of life (SF-36, etc.), and lean body mass.
Use standard mean differences if studies employ different scales.
Summarize adverse events (falls, fractures, delayed onset myalgia, etc.) based on original article definitions and perform meta-analysis if possible.
For crossover trials, use data from the first period only.

For cluster-RCTs (dichotomous data), apply the design effect and determine effective sample size/events using the intracluster correlation coefficient (ICC) per Cochrane Handbook (Chapter 16.3.5). For continuous data, reduce sample size only.

steps.title: Handle Missing Data and Statistics
steps.instruction: Address missing outcomes and statistics to ensure analysis robustness.

substeps.instruction: Request missing data from original authors.
Perform intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for all dichotomous data.
For continuous data, perform meta-analysis using available data from the original study without imputing missing data.

Calculate missing standard deviations (SD) using Altman’s method if only SE or p-value is reported. If unknown, calculate SD via t-value and confidence interval using Cochrane Handbook or other validated methods.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity and Bias
steps.instruction: Assess statistical heterogeneity and potential reporting/publication bias.

substeps.instruction: Visually inspect forest plots and calculate the I2 statistic (0-40%: not important; 30-60%: moderate; 50-90%: substantial; 75-100%: considerable).
For I2 > 50%, assess the reason for heterogeneity. Run Cochran’s Chi2 test (Q test) with significance at p < 0.10.
Assess publication bias via visual inspection of funnel plots and the Egger test (only if ≥ 10 trials or trials with similar sample sizes are present).
Cross-reference with ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP to identify unpublished trials.

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis and Subgroup Analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the final meta-analysis and explore effect modifiers.

substeps.instruction: Conduct meta-analysis using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4) with a random-effects model.
Perform subgroup analysis on primary outcomes based on: 1) Age (≥ 60 vs < 60 years), 2) Exercise type (strength training vs aerobic), and 3) Medication effect (if sample size permits).

steps.title: Conduct Sensitivity Analysis and Final Reporting
steps.instruction: Validate results through sensitivity analysis and generate a summary of findings.

substeps.instruction: Perform sensitivity analysis for primary outcomes by: 1) Excluding studies with high risk of bias (defined by inadequate allocation concealment, random sequence generation, or > 20% missing data), 2) Excluding cluster-RCTs, and 3) Comparing 95% CIs/fixed-effect pooled estimates vs 95% CIs/random-effects pooled estimates.
Generate a Summary of Findings table per the Cochrane Handbook.
Evaluate evidence quality using the GRADE approach, with K.H. deciding and T.K. finalizing the quality grade.
